title: Hold a live spoken conversation in my VoxCPM2 voice, and prove it turn by turn in the real app
why: One tap should open a conversation, not a single recording: I keep listening, every utterance becomes a message in the same thread, I write and then speak each answer, and I stop when someone talks over me. On a CPU my voice is about 5x slower than real time, so the proof also has to keep the browser and my voice worker on separate cores. This is how it was built and measured on 2026-11-26. On 2026-11-27 it became faster (compile, 8 steps, buffered streaming), learned to wait for unfinished thoughts, and was proven to stop mid-word when interrupted.

steps.title: Follow speak-with-voxcpm2 to install VoxCPM2 and fetch its weights
steps.why: Same worker, same weights. It encodes my reference once before READY, stops a sentence nobody will hear between two steps, compiles its diffusion estimator for this CPU (VOXCPM_COMPILE) and uses 8 diffusion steps (VOXCPM_TIMESTEPS; 8 measured equal to 10 for my voice, 6 was not).

steps.title: OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 taskset -c 2-3 .venv-voxcpm/bin/python services/voxcpm/server.py --port 8788 --warmup
steps.why: On a 4-core machine with a software-rendered browser, the browser needs two cores or its audio thread drops whole utterances, and it must not share my worker's cores. On a server (the browser is on the person's phone) give the worker every core: OMP_NUM_THREADS=4, about RTF 2.3.

steps.title: npm run build; bash scripts/live-conversation-serve.sh <log>
steps.why: Starts the built app with only Groq and Cerebras keys passed in, so no other model or voice can stand in for mine.

steps.title: node scripts/live-conversation-mic.cjs compose --dir docs/missions/live-voice-evidence/mic --spec "sil:20,a1,sil:80,a2,sil:80,a3,sil:70" --out <scenario.wav>
steps.why: Builds the conversation the test speaker will say: questions, silences, noise bursts. The clips are a synthetic voice, not a person and not me; say so wherever a result is reported. 'gen' makes new clips with a worker conditioned on a non-human reference.

steps.title: taskset -c 0,1 node scripts/verify-live-conversation.cjs --mic <scenario.wav> --out <dir> --label <name> [--mobile] [--type-at s|text] [--offline a-b] [--kill-worker-at s] [--restart-worker-at s] [--end-track-at s]
steps.why: Taps my microphone once and watches the whole session: messages as they appear, my states, every voice request with its headers and audio, media play/pause/ended, CPU and memory.

steps.title: node scripts/live-conversation-report.cjs <dir>/<name>.json
steps.why: Per turn: when the words ended, when I had them, when my answer was written, when I was heard, which engine spoke each sentence, and how many played to the end.

steps.title: node scripts/voice-live-latency-bench.cjs --worker http://127.0.0.1:8788 --out <dir> --steps 10,6,4
steps.why: Measures what my first word costs per text length and diffusion steps, and checks each clip through Whisper. Four steps garbled words. Six kept the words but added high-frequency energy on a long sentence. Eight matched ten on every measure, so I use eight.

steps.title: .venv-voxcpm/bin/python services/voxcpm/bench_step.py --out <dir> --threads 4 --variant <name> [--compile estimator] [--stream] [--steps 8]
steps.why: Stop the worker first (two copies do not fit in memory). Times every part of a generation step and saves the audio, so a speed-up can be checked against how I sound.

steps.title: .venv-voxcpm/bin/python services/voxcpm/score_similarity.py --dir <clips> --out <json>
steps.why: Scores clips against the parts of my recording the model never hears. A faster setting is only acceptable if this, Whisper's word accuracy and the high-frequency energy stay where 10 steps put them.

steps.title: node scripts/voice-latency-replay.cjs --run <run.json> --mode buffered --label <name> --out <dir>
steps.why: What a person would wait for on a whole server: page timings from a real browser run, my voice from the worker as it is configured now. Report it as a replay.

steps.title: A person talks with me on a desktop and an iPhone over HTTPS, interrupts me, types, and tells me whether it felt like a conversation
steps.why: No container has a microphone or a speaker, and only a person can judge pace and whether my voice sounds like me.
